name: str_split_i
title: Split up a string into pieces

origin.description: Split each string and return the i-th piece.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. The default interpretation is a regular expression. regex() sets the flags. fixed() compares literal text. coll() uses Unicode collation for a locale. boundary() matches character, word, line, and sentence boundaries. The empty string "" is equivalent to boundary("character").

arguments.name: i
arguments.text: Element to return. A negative value counts from the right. Zero is an error. A piece that is not there is NA.

origin.details: i is checked first, and it must be a whole number. A positive i calls str_split(string, pattern, simplify = NA, n = i + 1) and keeps column i. The extra piece is the unsplit remainder, so column i is one finished token. simplify NA pads a short row with NA, which is why a missing piece is NA rather than "". A negative i takes the absolute value, splits with the default n, and returns the piece that many places from the end, or NA when the split is shorter. i of 0 fails after the whole-number check, including when string and pattern have not been checked yet.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string and pattern. A missing piece is NA.
origin.example:
fruits <- c(
  "apples and oranges and pears and bananas",
  "pineapples and mangos and guavas"
)
str_split_i(fruits, " and ", 1)
str_split_i(fruits, " and ", 4)
str_split_i(fruits, " and ", -1)

translation.description: Split each string and return the i-th piece.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. None is an empty character vector.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Passed to str_split. A plain string is a regular expression. "" is a character boundary.

arguments.name: i
arguments.text: 1-based piece. Negative counts from the end. 0 raises ValueError. A fraction, Inf, and stringi._na.NA are not whole numbers. 1.0 and -1.0 are accepted.

translation.details: A positive i calls str_split with n = i + 1 and simplify equal to stringi._na.NA, then takes that column. The extra column holds the remainder, so the selected piece is not glued to the tail. A short row contributes NA. A negative i splits with the default n and indexes from the end. A string with fewer pieces is NA. The empty pattern on "" has no pieces, so both directions are NA.
translation.value: A list of strings the same length as the common size of string and pattern. A missing piece is stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.split import str_split_i

fruits = [
    "apples and oranges and pears and bananas",
    "pineapples and mangos and guavas",
]
print(str_split_i(fruits, " and ", 1))
print(str_split_i(fruits, " and ", 4))
print(str_split_i(fruits, " and ", -1))
